The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.

The container is labeled backend and already includes Python 3, Flask, uvicorn, celery and many backend tooling packages. For a minimal headless development environment Flask is lightweight, already present in the container, well suited to build REST endpoints, dashboards or simple web UIs for test plans and to integrate with test runners and Celery for asynchronous tasks.

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare workspace-local Python venv, ensure python3 exists, install python3-venv if needed, create .venv, upgrade pip/setuptools/wheel inside the venv, and write a minimal idempotent /etc/profile.d fragment only if content differs. Also create a project activation helper that sets FLASK_DEBUG for interactive sessions. Operates in the workspace path and avoids unnecessary global changes.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
PROFILE="/etc/profile.d/cdgh_env.sh"
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
# ensure python3 present (no sudo subshell)
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found" >&2; exit 2; }
# ensure python3-venv installed (only if import venv fails)
if ! python3 -c 'import venv' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y python3-venv -qq || { echo "failed to install python3-venv" >&2; exit 3; }
fi
# create venv if missing
if [ ! -d "$WS/.venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$WS/.venv"
fi
VENV="$WS/.venv"
# ensure pip tooling inside venv (minimize output)
"$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --upgrade pip setuptools wheel || { echo "venv pip tooling upgrade failed" >&2; exit 4; }
# minimal /etc/profile.d fragment written idempotently
TMPPROFILE="/tmp/cdgh_env.sh.$$"
cat > "$TMPPROFILE" <<EOF
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub environment (development)
export PROJECT_HOME="${WS}"
export ENABLE_CELERY=false
EOF
if ! sudo test -f "$PROFILE" || ! sudo cmp -s "$TMPPROFILE" "$PROFILE"; then
  sudo tee "$PROFILE" >/dev/null <"$TMPPROFILE"
  sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE"
fi
rm -f "$TMPPROFILE"
# create project-local activation helper (developer use)
cat > "$WS/activate_project.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
. "$WS/.venv/bin/activate"
export PROJECT_HOME="$WS"
export FLASK_DEBUG=1
export ENABLE_CELERY=false
SH
chmod +x "$WS/activate_project.sh"
# quick check: venv python usable
"$VENV/bin/python" -c "import sys; print('venv-ok', sys.version.split()[0])" >/dev/null 2>&1

steps.name: start
steps.description: Deterministically start the Flask dev server using the venv python in the background via setsid, write PID to $WS/run.pid and log to /tmp/cdgh_app.log. Using setsid ensures the captured PID is the server process and avoids races with intermediate shells. This step is reusable by validation and operators.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WS"
VENV="$WS/.venv"
LOG=/tmp/cdgh_app.log
PIDFILE="$WS/run.pid"
PORT=8000
# ensure no existing PID file or running process
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  OLDPID=$(cat "$PIDFILE") || true
  if [ -n "$OLDPID" ] && kill -0 "$OLDPID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "server already running (PID=$OLDPID)" >&2
    exit 6
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi
# start server deterministically with setsid and explicit venv python
setsid "$VENV/bin/python" -m flask run --host=127.0.0.1 --port=$PORT >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
# wait briefly to ensure process didn't exit immediately
sleep 0.5
if ! kill -0 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "server failed to start, see $LOG" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  exit 7
fi
echo "$PID" >"$PIDFILE"
echo "$PID"

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Full validation: ensure deps installed, start the app via the deterministic start step (or directly if necessary), verify readiness with a robust LISTEN check (IPv4/IPv6/wildcard-aware), fetch root and /health endpoints for evidence, then stop the server cleanly using the PID file. Provides clear evidence and logs on failure.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WS"
VENV="$WS/.venv"
# ensure deps present
"$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r requirements.txt pytest || { echo "deps install failed" >&2; exit 6; }
LOG=/tmp/cdgh_app.log
PORT=8000
HOST=127.0.0.1
PIDFILE="$WS/run.pid"
# robust port-in-use detection: check LISTEN entries for port across IPv4/IPv6
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ss -ltn "sport = :${PORT}" | grep -q LISTEN; then echo "port ${PORT} in use" >&2; exit 7; fi
elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if netstat -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "LISTEN.*:${PORT}\b" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "port ${PORT} in use" >&2; exit 7; fi
fi
# start server using start step and capture PID
"$WS"/start.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# try using start step script (if present) via invoking the plan start step script content
# prefer using PID file
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  SERVER_PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
else
  # fallback: start inline (deterministic)
  setsid "$VENV/bin/python" -m flask run --host=127.0.0.1 --port=$PORT >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
  SERVER_PID=$!
  echo "$SERVER_PID" >"$PIDFILE"
fi
# wait up to 10s for readiness
MAX_ATTEMPTS=10
ATTEMPT=0
until curl --silent --fail "http://${HOST}:${PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT+1))
  if [ $ATTEMPT -ge $MAX_ATTEMPTS ]; then
    echo "VALIDATION: server failed to start after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts" >&2
    echo "--- last log lines ---" >&2
    tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
    if [ -n "${SERVER_PID:-}" ]; then kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
    exit 8
  fi
  sleep 1
done
# server responsive - print brief evidence
echo "EVIDENCE: root=$(curl -sS http://${HOST}:${PORT}/ | head -c 200)"
echo "EVIDENCE: health=$(curl -sS http://${HOST}:${PORT}/health)"
# stop server gracefully using PID file
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE") || true
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 1
  if kill -0 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill -9 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  wait "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi
echo "VALIDATION: success"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WS"
VENV="$WS/.venv"
# ensure deps present
"$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r requirements.txt pytest || { echo "deps install failed" >&2; exit 6; }
LOG=/tmp/cdgh_app.log
PORT=8000
HOST=127.0.0.1
PIDFILE="$WS/run.pid"
# robust port-in-use detection
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ss -ltn "sport = :${PORT}" | grep -q LISTEN; then echo "port ${PORT} in use" >&2; exit 7; fi
elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if netstat -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "LISTEN.*:${PORT}\b" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "port ${PORT} in use" >&2; exit 7; fi
fi
# attempt to use start script
if [ -x "$WS/start.sh" ]; then
  "$WS/start.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
# prefer PID file
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  SERVER_PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
else
  setsid "$VENV/bin/python" -m flask run --host=127.0.0.1 --port=$PORT >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
  SERVER_PID=$!
  echo "$SERVER_PID" >"$PIDFILE"
fi
# wait for readiness up to 10s
MAX_ATTEMPTS=10
ATTEMPT=0
until curl --silent --fail "http://${HOST}:${PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT+1))
  if [ $ATTEMPT -ge $MAX_ATTEMPTS ]; then
    echo "VALIDATION: server failed to start after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts" >&2
    echo "--- last log lines ---" >&2
    tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
    if [ -n "${SERVER_PID:-}" ]; then kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
    exit 8
  fi
  sleep 1
done
# evidence
echo "EVIDENCE: root=$(curl -sS http://${HOST}:${PORT}/ | head -c 200)"
echo "EVIDENCE: health=$(curl -sS http://${HOST}:${PORT}/health)"
# stop server gracefully
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE") || true
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 1
  if kill -0 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill -9 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  wait "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi
echo "VALIDATION: success"
